narrative_purpose: Lets the reader see that a dying massive star is not uniform but a nest of concentric burning zones, with a dark inert centre that is the reason the whole structure is about to fail.
subject: A cutaway of a spherical star with a wedge removed so the interior is exposed. Inside, six nested concentric shells of clearly different colour and texture, from a broad diffuse outermost shell to progressively thinner, denser, brighter shells further in. At the very centre, a small distinctly dark, dense, dull sphere - the only unlit thing in the picture.
scene: The star hangs alone against empty dark space with a few faint distant stars. Fine wisps of gas drift off the outer surface.
camera: Straight-on view of the cutaway, the wedge opening toward the viewer so all shells are visible at once, star centred.
light: Self-luminous: each inner shell brighter and hotter-looking than the one outside it, glow spilling across the cut faces. The central sphere reflects nothing and stays dark against the brilliance around it.
palette: Outermost shells cool teal and cyan, middle shells brightening through mist-white, inner shells warm amber, the central sphere a dull desaturated stone grey - warm strictly confined to the inner shells.
style: Painterly naturalist cross-section plate, hand-rendered, soft-edged boundaries between shells rather than hard lines.
detail_level: Moderate: shell boundaries clearly readable as distinct zones, each with its own texture, but no hard outlines or engineering precision.
composition: Star centred and filling about two-thirds of the frame height. Empty dark space to the left and right of it for callouts.
consistency_notes: Six shells, no more - crowding them makes the picture unreadable. The dark centre must be unmistakably dark and unmistakably small relative to the shells.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no leader lines, no grid, no diagram chrome, no vector or flat-design look, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
